brief: A soldering station for my bench: a holder for the iron while it is switched on and hot, plus two bins for solder and spare tips.

requirements.requirement: holder for the iron while it is switched on and hot
requirements.evidence: Not built: Hex Cluster parts are 3D-printed plastic with no heat resistance rating; configurator checks fit only, not temperature or fire safety. A holder for a hot, powered soldering iron would risk melting, fire and burns, so no holder was placed. Built instead is cold storage for an unplugged iron (bins on bench).

requirements.requirement: two bins for solder and spare tips
requirements.evidence: bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full and bin:0,1,0~hex-bin-full on 3-cell base (piece:0,0,0, piece:1,0,0, piece:0,1,0); staged with solder-reel and tweezers to represent solder and tips compartments

finish.summary: Built a 3-cell bench organizer with two full-depth bins for solder and spare tips (staged with solder reel and tweezers). Declined the hot, powered iron holder: printed plastic cannot safely hold a hot soldering iron — use a commercial metal soldering-iron stand with heat shield for hot use, and use this organizer only for cold storage of the unplugged iron, solder and tips.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
